question: Excluding stoppages, the speed of a bus is 60 kmph and including stoppages, it is 54 kmph. For how many minutes does the bus stop per hour?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Stoppage time per hour = (Faster Speed − Slower Speed) ÷ Faster Speed

Stoppage time = (60 − 54) ÷ 60

Stoppage time = 6 ÷ 60 hour

Stoppage time in minutes = (1/10) × 60 = 6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 6 mins.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed without stoppages = 60 kmph

Speed with stoppages = 54 kmph

 
• 
 
• 

 Without Stoppage (Speed: 60 kmph)
 
 Distance: 60 km in 60 mins
 
 With Stoppage (Speed: 54 kmph)
 
 Distance: 54 km

 
 Stop

 

 6 km gap
 Takes 6 mins

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ In 1 hour (60 mins), without stoppages, the bus covers a distance of 60 km.

⇒ In 1 hour (60 mins), with stoppages, the bus covers a distance of 54 km.

⇒ Loss in distance due to stoppages = 60 − 54 = 6 km.

⇒ Time required to cover this 6 km gap at the original speed is the actual stoppage time.

⇒ Stoppage time = Distance ÷ Original Speed

⇒ Stoppage time = 6 ÷ 60 hours = 1/10 hours.

⇒ Stoppage time in minutes = (1/10) × 60 = 6 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 mins.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

When equal distances are covered at speeds S₁ and S₂, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂). For equal time intervals, Average Speed = (S₁ + S₂) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed

For two bodies moving in the same direction, relative speed is |S₁ − S₂|. For bodies moving in opposite directions, it is S₁ + S₂.

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert kmph to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s to kmph, multiply the value by 18/5.
